item.title: 8-month Iran war looms large over Israeli election
item.description: Israeli voters are choosing their next government, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu insisting only he can finish the job started eight months ago in Iran.

item.title: In Trump's pardon economy, victims lost out on $119M in restitution
item.description: Small businesses and retirees are left empty-handed as fraudsters, some represented by Trump allies, win clemency.

item.title: TikTok parent ByteDance's founder is China's richest person again
item.description: The founder of Tiktok parent ByteDance, Zhang Yiming, reclaimed the top spot on a list of China's richest people, driven by his company's push into AI.

item.title: John Thune's balancing act: Inside his push to save the GOP majority
item.description: Senate Majority Leader John Thune has tried to balance passing the president's agenda and preserving the independence of the Senate. The midterms are his biggest test yet.

item.title: Hospital beds for the nation's sickest kids are disappearing
item.description: Hospitals nationwide are cutting intensive services for kids in critical care. Many cite too few patients, staffing shortages, and money problems.

item.title: These factors could decide Netanyahu's fate in Israel's election
item.description: Israelis are choosing their next government. The race is wide open, and Benjamin Netanyahu's political fate could hinge on a couple key factors.

item.title: DOJ takes steps to charge James Comey again
item.description: The DOJ took steps to charge James Comey with leaking information earlier this month, in its third attempt to bring criminal charges against the former FBI director and Trump foe.

item.title: Judge continues to block Trump from cutting down trees at D.C. golf course
item.description: "The Court earlier stated, 'I am not the Lorax. I do not speak for the trees,'" U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes wrote. "The Court still does not speak for the trees. It speaks only for the rule of law."

item.title: Jay-Z to headline 2027 Super Bowl halftime show
item.description: The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Monday night that Jay-Z will be the featured performer for the halftime festivities on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

item.title: Eric Bauza, actor who voiced Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, dies at 46
item.description: Eric Bauza, the Emmy-winning actor who voiced iconic "Looney Tunes" characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, died on Sunday, according to his manager. He was 46.

item.title: Dollar General overcharged people at checkout for years, FTC says
item.description: The discount retailer routinely charges customers more at checkout than the prices it displays on shelves, price tags and ads, according to federal and state authorities.

item.title: Video of police being called to youth soccer game draws outrage
item.description: One of the league's directors said the parents were being disruptive, but 3-year-old Nevada's mother said, "They're literally kicking him out of this place because he's good at soccer."

item.title: 7-year-old yoga instructor sets record
item.description: Phoenix Giselle Hicks was certified as a yoga instructor before her 6th birthday. Now, the 7-year-old is in the Guinness Book of World Records as the youngest female yoga instructor. Tony Dokoupil reports.

item.title: Parents claim 3-year-old was kicked out of soccer league for being too good
item.description: Police were called to a youth soccer game that featured a star 3-year-old. The parents claim their son was being punished for being too good, but a league director said it was the parents who were being disruptive. Cristian Benavides has the story.

item.title: Netanyahu faces first national election since Oct. 7, 2023
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing his country's first national election since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas terror attack. Matt Gutman takes a look at what's at stake and who might unseat Netanyahu.

item.title: Flooding hits both coasts
item.description: Both coasts are dealing with flooding. In the West, El Niño and full moon tides are bringing rising water, while the East is dealing with what's known as the King Tide. Rob Marciano has the latest.

item.title: Manhunt underway for escaped murderer in Tennessee
item.description: Jacob Morley, a convicted murderer, escaped from a medium security prison in Tennessee over the weekend. Authorities are asking local residents to check their home security cameras for any sign of the escapee. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: Trump, Obama hold rallies ahead of midterms
item.description: President Trump is holding several rallies, including in deep-red states, in the week before the midterm as he tries to keep his party in control of Congress. Former President Barack Obama is also headlining events, hoping to help flip control to the Democrats. Weijia Jiang reports and Robert Costa joins for analysis.

item.title: High gas prices could put Texas in play for Democrats
item.description: With the midterms just over a week away, many Texas voters are expressing concerns about high costs, especially for gas. Those concerns are leading some to believe James Talarico has a shot at becoming the first Democrat elected statewide in Texas since 1994. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: LA residents sue city over Hollywood sign crowds: "Reached its peak"
item.description: A group of residents who live near the world-famous Hollywood Sign, which attracts millions of visitors from around the world every year, have filed public nuisance lawsuits against the city of Los Angeles, asking officials to do more.

item.title: Why DOJ's attempt to charge James Comey again is highly unusual
item.description: The Department of Justice took steps to charge former FBI director James Comey for the third time on Monday. CBS News senior Justice Department reporter Sarah Lynch explains why the situation is so unusual.

item.title: Legal analysis of DOJ taking steps to charge James Comey again
item.description: The Trump administration is attempting to charge former FBI director James Comey again. Comey said he remains innocent. CBS News legal contributor Rebecca Roiphe has more.

item.title: Venezuelan officials allowed Maria Corina Machado to return, Rubio says
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Venezuela's interim government told the U.S. "weeks and weeks" earlier that opposition leader Maria Corina Machado could return to the country without interference.

item.title: Mississippi voters express desire for change as Trump visits red state
item.description: President Trump is visiting Mississippi on Monday, a historically bright-red state that he won in 2024, when he gained more than 60% of the vote. Ashton Pittman, a news editor for the Mississippi Free Press, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss the midterm elections there.

item.title: 10/26: CBS Evening News
item.description: Texas sees a down-to-the-wire Senate race; Trump goes on a campaign blitz in a Republican stronghold.

item.title: 10/26: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: President Trump amps up rhetoric against El-Sayed; Israel is holding its first Parliamentary elections since the Oct. 7, 2023 attacks.

item.title: Bishops lament White House meeting that produced photo with Trump
item.description: Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret about agreeing to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Trump.

item.title: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 workers as it invests more in AI
item.description: Roughly a quarter of Microsoft's workforce will be eligible for a "voluntary exit offer" as the company tries to shed workers.

item.title: Consumers face scarier Halloween costs this year. Here's why.
item.description: Americans are forecast to spend a record $13.5 billion on Halloween this year, with the average consumer shelling out hundreds of dollars.

item.title: Why Are We All So Thirsty For Reality TV Again? | Straight Up with Kelly and Vlad
item.description: "Dancing With the Stars" is breaking voting records even after 35 seasons, cringe "Love Is Blind" clips are breaking the internet, and "Love Island" is still breaking hearts week after week. It seems we are having a reality TV renaissance. But what's behind it? Are we yearning for people to be "real" and "messy" in an online world so otherwise polished? Or are we falling for a trap? Is reality TV the furthest thing from reality of all? Vlad and Kelly are breaking it down in the very first episode of Straight Up. We love a good cocktail on this show, but please drink responsibly: this content is for listeners 21 and over, so know your limits, enjoy in moderation, and always plan a safe ride home.
